_comment: The Flydigi 'V1' family via a 2.4 GHz receiver (VID 04b4, PID 2412; Direwolf 3 and others). The data does NOT come through gamepad interface 0, but through the vendor USB interface 2 (usage page 0xFFA0; on Linux it is usually the receiver's third hidraw): first a 12-byte information request must be sent, after which the receiver starts sending reports with Report ID 04 and byte 0xFE. The protocol and offsets are taken from the open SDL driver (src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_flydigi.c, the V1 branch), not measured on this device: check with `gamepad-remapd monitor /dev/hidrawN` and fix if needed. All offsets/bytes are indexes into the read() array, i.e. including the Report ID byte (byte 0).
name: Flydigi V1 2.4G (04b4:2412, vendor iface 2)

handshake._note: GET_INFO: report 05, command EC. The receiver answers with report 04 with byte 15 = EC (sync filters it out) and starts sending the state.

EXTRA1._note: SDL: two extra bits (C/Z) only on some models; which of them is C and which is Z is not confirmed

PAD_UP._note: The D-pad here is a bit mask of directions (UP=1, RIGHT=2, DOWN=4, LEFT=8; a diagonal = the sum), not an 8-position hat

_rumble_note: There is no rumble here on purpose: in DInput mode the receiver does not serve the interface OUT endpoint (usbmon: even SDL, which sends GET_INFO 05 EC, gets only a timeout, -ETIMEDOUT). Every write would block for seconds. Flydigi rumble works in XInput mode (xpad, evdev FF).
